ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text: As shown in the figure, two lines $l_1$ and $l_2$ passing through point $A(2, 0)$ intersect the $y$-axis at points $B$ and $C$, respectively, where point $B$ is above the origin and point $C$ is below the origin. It is known that $AB = \sqrt{13}$. What are the coordinates of point $B$?
ready1_open_rewrite.raw_answer_text:
\textbf{Solution:} Given that $\because A(2,0)$, \\
$\therefore OA=2$, \\
In the right-angled triangle $Rt\triangle AOB$, $\angle AOB=90^\circ$, \\
$OB=\sqrt{AB^{2}-OA^{2}}=\sqrt{13-4}=3$, \\
$\therefore$ the coordinates of point B are $\boxed{(0,3)}$.
